Messages.Author: Damnans
Messages.Body:
The goal of this to-be-determined reward system is not only to encourage participation in V:EKN sanctioned tournaments but to increase the rate of archon and tournament winning deck submissions as well.

So here are some ideas about possible rewards based on different factors:

Continental Championship automatic qualification
The top X% players (rounded up) in each national ranking get automatic qualification for any Continental Championship (only for Day 1, if any).

A player's portrait on a VTES card
This prize is meant for players who have accomplished special feats, such as winning a Continental Championship.

Alternative Halls of Fame hosted on vekn.net
In addition to hosting Jeff Thompson's Hall of Fame on vekn.net, I suggest the creation of other kind of Halls of Fame for other extraordinary feats such as:
- Winning the most tournaments with a given clan: e.g., Clan Loyalty Hall of Fame
- Winning tournaments with the most different clans: Diversity Hall of Fame
- Winning a tournament with a given difficult-to-win-with clan: Strangers Among Us Hall of Fame
- Winning a tournament with an extremely difficult-to-win-with deck (e.g. Samedi vote deck): Blessing of Chaos Hall of Fame
- Winning the most tournaments with rush decks: Monsters Hall of Fame
- Winning the most tournaments with wall decks: Wall of Fame
- Winning the most tournaments with vote decks: Masters of Politics Hall of Fame
- Winning the most tournaments with bleed decks: Masters of Bleed Hall of Fame
- The player with the most VPs in a tournament (in the last 18 months): Capitalist Hall of Fame
- The player with the most GWs in a tournament (in the last 18 months): Play-to-Win Hall of Fame
- Etc...

Any comments, improvements, suggestions?

V:EKN Website Coordinator

Messages.Author: ICL
Messages.Body:
The alternate Hall of Fames sound really bad. Small sample size, dilution of what it means to be a HoFer, increased arbitrariness are some problems I see.

Keep in mind that the TWDA criteria for what constitutes a deck of a particular clan are already easily "abused". Five copies of one vampire is not a deck of a clan. 5/5/x/y or 6/6 is not a clan deck. My "Toreador" deck with 7 of 21 being Toreador is not a clan deck. But, they all qualify because determining what it means to really be of a clan is subjective.

People already get credit for winning with unusual stuff. What the TWDA and HoF do is stay relatively objective, leaving the playerbase to recognize or not "secret achievements". And, while the difficulty of either winning tournaments or making it into the HoF changes over time independent of the requirements, the difficulty of what constitutes "hard to win with" and the like varies far more. Gangrel used to have tons of wins, not so much the case anymore. Kiasyd had a surprisingly low number of wins for the longest time given that Dominate + stealth works every once in a while. See Guruhi before Nana and after Nana.

Traveller Card Game

Messages.Author: ICL
Messages.Body:
It's tempting to say that if the idea is to call out cool decks, just call out cool decks. Post their links. Say something about them. Remind people every year or so that there was this really cool deck.

However, that's not an organized way to do it. I can see someone managing a place for recognizing the coolest decks of all time. I can see that being called the Decks Hall of Fame or some such.

But, create a poll for that sort of thing. Put up all of the decks from a given year or for a given category that Jeff used to break up decks (clan, capacity, number of entrants).

I just can't imagine trying to institute a bunch of arbitrary categories. Categorizing decks can be hard, if for no other reason, and I see other reasons.

Btw, candidate for coolest deck of all time and certainly way cooler than my tournament winning Baali deck: thelasombra.com/decks/twd.htm#2k3watfordmarch
